title: Names
summary: The year of the columns: three hours a night on the Chamber floor saying sixteen slabs until he can say them in the dark; six hundred and forty-one, four hundred with nothing beside the number, one with a tree, which is Corr's. The Master's seal drawn in the margin and drilled from the palm. Tremor reaches a heart through rock: the old man's, catching on the third. The autumn inspection: six hours in the doorway, void, the same young Flamen frowns and writes for the second time, his heart going fast through the rock; a note the first time, a pattern the second; a file for a man in a grey coat. Winter: the Censor dies on the shelf with the arithmetic done first. Four things: the slabs are a copy and Jonah is the book; carry me through the tunnel and put me against the wall I drew, so Tullus finds a locked room and lies awake; write me last as well and say me on the road; and the fourth, the thing he never taught: it is not a suit, it is someone, it has been polite for five years to a man who calls it a thing, ask it what it wants before it asks you. Jonah says the sixteenth slab with the endings right. 'Sertorius.' The heart catches on the second and stays. He carries him through the tunnel, lays him against the wall, and the count goes through: one more. He seals the tunnel from inside so it is rock, takes the half chisel, leaves the stick across the shelf, writes the name below the tree and the seal, locks the door from the road. Six hundred and forty-two on the road. He tells the genius he is sorry he did not ask, and it turns and looks at him. The place where it can answer is down.
story_date: 393-394, the end of the fifth year and the winter of the sixth

events.description: The year of the columns: the sixteen slabs memorized, six hundred and forty-one names, four hundred numbers with nothing, Corr's tree. The Master's seal drawn in the sixteenth slab's margin and drilled from the palm until it comes before he finishes asking.
Tremor reaches a heart through rock: the Censor's, catching on the third in summer, on the second by winter. 'That is the last arithmetic I have and it comes out to the winter.'

The sixth-year College inspection in autumn: the big glass, four Flamens, six hours in the doorway, void; the same young Flamen frowns and writes for the second time, heart going fast. The Censor: a note the first time, a pattern the second; a file; a Frumentarius will read it one day.

The Censor's four things on the shelf: the slabs are a copy and Jonah is the book; put me against the wall I drew and let Tullus find a locked room; write me last as well and say me on the road; and the untaught thing: it is not a suit, it is someone, it has been polite for five years, ask it what it wants before it asks you.

The Censor dies on the shelf after hearing the sixteenth slab said with the endings right. His last word is 'Sertorius', said to Jonah as a name for the only time. His heart catches on the second and does not come off it.

Jonah carries the Censor through the tunnel to the Cradle and lays him against the wall he drew; the wall takes him from the hole where a Tribune's genius was; the count goes through: one more, between a Halyard sailor and a man with no name. The genius watches from the doorway, unafraid and unhungry.

Jonah seals the tunnel from the Chamber side so the seam is rock; takes the half-worn chisel; leaves the stick across the empty shelf; cuts the name below the tree and the seal on the sixteenth slab and says it aloud; locks the door from the road with his hand.

Ulli heard the wall go quiet for a breath. 'He said the road was the only thing he'd drawn that he'd have liked to walk.' Jonah says all six hundred and forty-two on the road and the first name at the top.
Jonah tells the genius, in the old tongue, that he knows it is someone and is sorry he did not ask; it turns in the doorway and looks at him, not through him. The place where it can answer is down.

knowledge_changes.fact: He is the book: sixteen slabs, six hundred and forty-two names, said in the dark without a fault.
The genius is someone, not a suit; it has been polite for five years; ask it what it wants before it asks you.
The young Flamen has written him twice, at seventeen and at thirty; a note the first time, a pattern the second; it will go in a file a Frumentarius will read.
Tremor can read a heart through rock.
The Censor is dead, given to the wall he drew, counted, written last on the sixteenth slab, said on the road.
The Master's seal comes from his palm before he finishes asking.
The Censor is dead; the wall went quiet a breath; he said a name that was not his.
A cut convict on the Shallows read as void with something wrong on the glass in the fourth-year inspection; he wrote it down.
The same convict read void with a wobble again in the sixth year: a pattern.

thread_beats.description: Dies with the arithmetic done. Given to the wall he drew and counted by it. Tullus will find a locked room. 'Sertorius.'
Jonah is the book. The Censor written first and last. Six hundred and forty-two said on the road.
The untaught thing: it is someone, polite, never asked. Jonah says sorry; it turns and looks at him. The answer is down.
The young Flamen writes him twice: a pattern; a file; a man in a grey coat with no stripe.
The Master's seal drilled. Tremor to a heart. The tunnel sealed. The Chamber's numbers end with the Censor: Tullus's galleries have no arithmetic now.
The Form against the air, corrected from the shelf. Do not read hearts at dinner; it gets you challenged, and you cannot spoil on a floor.
The wall goes quiet for a breath counting the man who drew the room. The genius watches unafraid. Down.

clues.description: The Chamber's monthly numbers end with the Censor; Tullus will find a locked room with sixteen slabs and no one.
clues.mechanism: Tullus's galleries have no arithmetic; the harvest is rushed and the guard is thin (ch.26, ch.29).

clues.description: The slabs go up the Throat to the College's vault as a copy.
clues.mechanism: Book 2: the slabs in the College vault; Livia reads them.

clues.description: The genius turned and looked at him, not through him.
clues.mechanism: Ch.23 the Mouth is where it can answer; ch.31 'Name.'

clues.description: 'Do not tell anyone at dinner what their heart is doing.'
clues.mechanism: Book 2: Tremor at Vibian tables; Livia's heart.

clues.description: The stick left across the empty shelf.
clues.mechanism: Ch.30: 'the old man's stick broken' (Sabinus's fang across it; Jonah takes it on harvest day).

clues.description: The seal from the palm before he finishes asking.
clues.mechanism: Ch.26 forges the manifest's seal; Book 2 opens the columbarium.

new_objects.name: The half chisel
new_objects.description: The Censor's chisel worn to half its length over nine years of tunnel. Jonah took it.
new_objects.significance: The only thing of the old man's he carries.

character_emotional_states.emotional_state: The book. Said the first name on the road. Sorry he did not ask. Going down.
Heard the wall go quiet for a breath.
Wrote it twice. A pattern. Heart going fast.

scenes.summary: The year of the columns; the seal in the margin; Tremor to a heart.
The autumn inspection; six hours; the frown; the pattern.
Four things; the sixteenth slab; Sertorius; the heart on the second.
Through the tunnel; the wall takes him; counted; the tunnel sealed; the name cut; the road; sorry I did not ask; it looks at him; down.

opening_hook: The old man made him read the slabs until he could say them in the dark, and then he made him say them in the dark, and then he died.
closing_hook: There is a place where it can answer, and he thinks he knows where it is. Down.
notes: The Censor dead, given to the wall. Jonah holds all sixteen slabs in memory; the physical slabs remain in the locked Chamber for Tullus's men to find. Tunnel sealed. Stick left on the shelf. Grade about 28. Sixth-year inspection passed (Pollio's second note). Ch.23 the Mouth: the genius's answer; ch.24 the name.
